problem:
The velocity of a particle is $(-3i+5j)\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}.$ If the particle moves with a constant acceleration of $(2i-j)\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ find the velocity of the particle when $t=4\,\text{s}.$

$v=($
{{field-1}}$i$
$+$
{{field-2}}$j\,)\,\text{m/s}$
worked_solution:
Recall that when a particle moves with constant acceleration, the velocity vector at time $t$ can be found using

$$
v=u+at,
$$

where $u$ is the initial velocity, and $a$ is the acceleration of the particle.

Here, we have

$$
u=-3i+5j,\,a=2i-j.
$$

Therefore, after $t=4\,\text{s},$ the velocity of the particle will be

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =u+at \\  & =(-3i+5j)+(2i-j)(4) \\  & =(-3i+5j)+(8i-4j) \\  & =(5i+1j)\,\text{m/s}.\end{aligned}
$$
